answer: Attention-Debt Registration: an identity activates only after its key spends a fixed interval answering unpredictable micro-challenges issued at random times. Like tending a vine, each identity must be continuously pruned by real-time responses; missed windows suspend it. The attacker's cost is parallel human or model attention per identity, sustained indefinitely—scaling linearly, unlike one-time fees. A willow of decoy accounts cannot be cheaply grown, and each harvested nectar of eligibility requires fresh attention, making mass registration economically irrational.
